correctness.rationale: Coprimality gives x=b(k−t), y=at with 0≤t≤k. For interior t the three coprimality tests in (1) are necessary and sufficient by considering which factors a common prime divides; the two endpoints have gcd>1. I checked the prime-power argument and all four exceptional cases (7, 11, 13, 15), including the split on 3|b at 11. An independent exhaustive check colors every prime <k by membership in a, b, or neither; larger primes cannot affect an interior solution. It found no obstruction for k=2..15, and six obstructing colorings out of 729 at 16. Direct enumeration of 240240=273x+55y gave 17 nonnegative solutions, none primitive. Multiplying 55 by m coprime to 273 preserves both coprimality of the generators and each obstruction. Replay: /workspace/replays/recheck_frozen.py, primitive(). This is not a claim about larger k or arbitrary targets.
